N-2.1-A.skill: locate a defect in the endomembrane secretory pathway from the order and timing of radioactive label.

N-2.1-B.skill: match a drug or mutation affecting one cytoskeletal element to the cellular process it disrupts.

N-2.2-A.skill: use supply proportional to surface area and demand proportional to volume to predict whether a cell of a given size can meet its needs.

N-2.2-B.skill: compare the total surface area of one large cell with that of many small cells containing the same total volume.

N-2.3-A.skill: interpret a cell-fusion or fluorescence experiment as evidence about lateral movement of membrane components.

N-2.3-B.skill: determine which side of a membrane a protein domain faces from enzyme or antibody accessibility data.

N-2.4-A.skill: predict relative permeability of a pure phospholipid bilayer from molecular size, charge, and polarity using a data table.

N-2.4-B.skill: use control preparations to attribute selective transport of a polar substance to a membrane protein rather than to the bilayer.

N-2.5-A.skill: classify a transport process as passive or active from time-course data on solute concentration and the effect of an energy inhibitor.

N-2.5-B.skill: explain dynamic equilibrium: at equal concentrations, solute still crosses in both directions at equal rates with no net movement.

N-2.6-A.skill: interpret rate versus concentration data to identify carrier-mediated transport and predict the effect of changing carrier number.

N-2.6-B.skill: explain that a transport protein for passive transport changes how fast equilibrium is reached but not the equilibrium concentration.

N-2.7-A.skill: predict the direction of water movement by combining solute potential and pressure potential into water potential.

N-2.7-B.skill: infer the tonicity relationship and the osmoregulatory work an organism must do from data on its response in different solutions.

N-2.8-A.skill: explain how a gradient built by an ATP-driven pump powers coupled transport of a second solute.

N-2.8-B.skill: predict the effects on membrane area, vesicle supply, and secretion when endocytosis or exocytosis is blocked.

N-2.9-A.skill: calculate how confining molecules in a small compartment raises their concentration and the rate of a concentration-dependent reaction.

N-2.9-B.skill: assign organelles to fractions of a centrifuged homogenate from the biochemical activities in each fraction.

N-2.10-A.skill: interpret molecular sequence, antibiotic, or genome data as evidence for the endosymbiotic origin of mitochondria and chloroplasts.

N-2.10-B.skill: sort organelles by proposed origin (endosymbiosis or membrane infolding) from a table of features.
